pairs.why: Both calculator bodies are built soundly and both lack an '=' key. B is marginally closer to the real card because its dark keys and wide 0 key match the real keypad layout.
A's keypad has numbered and operator keys, while B's keys are blank cubes, so B's calculator could not be used.
A hangs flat on the wall like the real clock, while B's round clock stands on its curved rim on the floor with no stand or foot to hold it up.
In A the lifebuoy hangs from a hook on the post and the rope is coiled around a piling, while in B the lifebuoy and the rope strung between posts float in front of the deck with unclear attachment.
B is a wall clock mounted flat like the real card, while A's round clock balances on its rim on a floor with no stand.
A is a believable coil with one loop pulled out and tied with a red wrap, while in B a separate closed ring is joined to the coil by a bead and the rope does not run continuously.
A's armrests sit on posts and its X-legs pivot at visible hinges under a seat they support, while B's front X-frame and rear legs connect to the seat sling less clearly.
Both ropes repeat the same broken idea, a coil plus a closed ring joined by a bead, so neither one reads as a single continuous rope.
